name: Western Addition A-1 (Geary corridor, Japantown south of Post)
note: Established 28 May 1956 (108 acres, 'irregular area of 27 blocks'); early clearance between Franklin (E), Post (N), St. Joseph's Ave (W) and Eddy (S); ~8,000 residents evicted; Geary Expressway demolition 1960; St. Francis Square occupied 1964, Japan Center built 1965-68. clear_end ESTIMATE 1963. Ring = the four bounding streets (the real area is irregular: some blocks inside the box were not cleared). Confidence MEDIUM for extent, MEDIUM for dates. NOTE: a few landmarks inside survived (e.g. Buchanan YMCA 1926, churches); apply the rule only to buildings without an exact assessor year.

name: Western Addition A-2 (Bush to Grove, Broderick to Van Ness)
note: A-2 plan adopted 1964: 'seventy blocks and 277 acres surrounding the A-1 area and extending from Bush to Grove streets and from Broderick Street to Van Ness Avenue' (Japantown HCS 2009). Mass clearance mostly late 1960s-early 1970s (clear_start/end ESTIMATED 1966-1973); new housing (Plaza East rebuild, Fillmore Center 1988-90, Buchanan Mall 1976) followed into the 1990s. The ring is the outer rectangle and CONTAINS A-1 (apply A-1 first / treat A-1 as a hole). Unlike A-1, A-2 retained or relocated many Victorians (rehabilitation programme; Cottage Row etc.), so apply the clearance rule only to footprints with imputed/spike years. Confidence MEDIUM.

name: Golden Gateway / Embarcadero Center (old Produce Market)
note: The wholesale produce district (post-1906 2-4 storey brick warehouses and commission houses) was cleared for the Golden Gateway project from c.1960; produce dealers moved to the new terminal at Jerrold Ave (Islais Creek) in 1963; Golden Gateway Center towers 1963-67, Alcoa/Maritime Plaza 1964-67, Embarcadero Center 1971-82, Hyatt Regency 1973. Ring: Broadway-Battery-Sacramento-Drumm/California-The Embarcadero. Dates and south edge ESTIMATED (LOW-MEDIUM confidence); the Colombo Market arch on Front St was kept as an archway.

name: Yerba Buena Center (South of Market)
note: 87-acre SFRA project active 1966-2009 (plans from 1953). Residential hotels (SROs), flats and light industry cleared mostly 1966-1975 despite the TOOR lawsuits (clear_end ESTIMATED 1977); Moscone South 1981, Marriott 1989, Yerba Buena Gardens 1993/1998. Ring ESTIMATED (LOW-MEDIUM): Mission St 2nd-5th with the Market St frontage between 3rd and 4th, south to Harrison. Survivors inside include the Old Mint (1874), St. Patrick's Church and the Jessie St substation - apply only to buildings without exact assessor years.

name: Diamond Heights
note: SFRA project active 1948-1978 on mostly undeveloped hillside (few prior buildings); grading and street building c.1955-62, houses and towers from the early 1960s. Ring approximated from Portola/Clipper/Douglass/Diamond St and the Glen Canyon edge (LOW confidence). Use it mainly to stop modern houses from being imputed to pre-1955 years.

name: Hunters Point Hill (Hunters Point Redevelopment Project, war housing)
note: WWII temporary war housing for shipyard workers on Hunters Point hill (built 1942-45, ~20,000 residents by 1945) was replaced under the SFRA Hunters Point project (active from 1969); demolition of the temporary dwellings ran from the late 1960s into the 1970s. Dates ESTIMATED; ring hand-drawn around the hill (LOW confidence).

name: India Basin Industrial Park (Butchertown)
note: Former Butchertown meat-processing district turned into an industrial park, project started 1968. Ring: Cargo Way - Jennings St - Evans Ave - Third St (ESTIMATED from the neighbourhood extent; LOW-MEDIUM confidence). Dates ESTIMATED.

name: Rincon Point - South Beach
note: SFRA Rincon Point-South Beach project (active 1970s-1988): waterfront warehouses, rail spurs and the State Belt yard between Mission St and China Basin cleared in the 1980s for South Beach housing (from 1987), the South Beach marina and Rincon Center (1988). Ring: Mission/Spear-Steuart - The Embarcadero - King - 2nd - Bryant - Spear. Dates ESTIMATED (1980-1987); LOW-MEDIUM confidence. Historic Rincon Annex post office (1940) survived.

name: Transbay (1939 terminal, ramps and adjacent parcels)
note: Transbay Redevelopment Area (2005): the 1939 Transbay Terminal closed Aug 2010 and was demolished 2010-11, its bus ramps by 2012; ramp-side parcels (parking, warehouses) then sold for towers. Ring: Mission 2nd-Beale, Beale-Folsom, Folsom to Essex/Harrison, back to 2nd. The terminal and ramps themselves are modelled separately (transbay_terminal_1939). Dates from the transit-center history; ring ESTIMATED (MEDIUM).

name: Chinatown - Ping Yuen site (Pacific Ave)
note: SFHA cleared Chinatown tenements on the south side of Pacific Ave (Grant to beyond Stockton) for Ping Yuen: construction contract 1950, Central Ping Yuen dedicated 21 Oct 1951, East/West by 1956; North Ping Yuen (north side of Pacific, dedicated 1961) is not included. Ring hand-drawn along the south frontage (LOW-MEDIUM).

name: Bay Bridge approach viaduct through SoMa (I-80, 5th St - anchorage)
note: Right of way between Harrison and Bryant cleared for the elevated approach built with the bridge (construction 1933-36, opened 12 Nov 1936). Corridor = route buffered 35 m (MEDIUM confidence for alignment, dates ESTIMATED from bridge construction).

name: Skyway (I-80 / US 101 link, 5th St - 10th St)
note: Freeway link between the Bayshore/James Lick Fwy and the Bay Bridge approach, opened 1955 (route record). Clearance window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 30 m.

name: James Lick Freeway (US 101, Augusta St - Central Fwy junction)
note: First SF freeway: Augusta-25th St opened June 1951, north to the junction 1953 (route record). Takings along Potrero Ave/Bayshore through flats and industry; window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 35 m.

name: Central Freeway south of Market (US 101 junction - Mission St - Market)
note: Double-deck viaduct: to Mission St opened 1 Mar 1955, to Market Apr 1959 (route record); takings along the Duboce/13th St corridor. Window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 30 m.

name: Central Freeway north of Market (Octavia, Market - Turk/Golden Gate)
note: Opened Apr 1959 over the Octavia alignment through Hayes Valley; Victorian rows cleared for it (removed 1992/2003, now Octavia Blvd). Window ESTIMATED; alignment north of Fell LOW confidence (per route record); corridor buffered 30 m.

name: Embarcadero Freeway (SR 480)
note: Opened 5 Feb 1959, mostly built over The Embarcadero and Belt Railroad tracks, with some warehouse takings near the Bay Bridge end. Window ESTIMATED; alignment approximate (as in the landmark model); corridor buffered 25 m. LOW confidence that much was cleared.

name: Southern Freeway I-280 (Daly City - Alemany Maze)
note: Built c.1965 on the old SP Ocean View branch / Alemany alignment through Ocean View, Mission Terrace and Glen Park (opening year ESTIMATED in the route record). Window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 40 m.

name: I-280 Alemany Maze - Mariposa St
note: Built north toward 18th St by 1969 (route record, ESTIMATED) through Bernal/Bayview edge and Potrero (Pennsylvania Ave). Window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 40 m.

name: I-280 Mariposa St - King St (incl. demolished 3rd St stub)
note: Completed to 3rd St in 1973 through Dogpatch/Mission Bay industrial land and SP yards (route record). Window ESTIMATED; corridor buffered 35 m. Prior fabric mixes warehouses and rail_yards.

name: Mission Bay (SP / Santa Fe rail yards, freight sheds, warehouses)
note: Mission Bay Redevelopment Plans (North and South) adopted 1998 (Catellus, former Southern Pacific / Santa Fe land): the rail yards, freight sheds and warehouses between Townsend/King St, 7th St / I-280, Mariposa St and the bay were cleared from 1998 (UCSF Mission Bay groundbreaking 1999, first housing c.2001-03); some yard buildings lingered into the mid-2000s. Ring: Townsend & 7th - Townsend & 4th - King & 3rd - China Basin - Terry Francois & Mariposa - Owens & Mariposa - 7th & 16th (street intersections from DataSF centerlines). Dates ESTIMATED (1998-2008); MEDIUM confidence.

name: Park Center Plaza (San José Redevelopment Agency's first project, west of Market St)
note: Declared blighted by the City Council 25 Feb 1960; redevelopment plan adopted 24 Jul 1961; 'thirteen blocks in the west-of-Market neighborhood' to be leveled for a high-rise commercial centre; groundbreaking Jul 1968, most buildings completed by 1972 (Park Center Financial Plaza, Center for the Performing Arts 1972). The 1961 building survey covers Almaden, Locust, S Market, Park, Post, S River, W San Carlos, W San Fernando and Vine. clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED (between plan adoption and groundbreaking). Ring = Market x San Fernando, Market x San Carlos, San Carlos at the Guadalupe (SR 87), San Fernando at the Guadalupe: extent LOW-MEDIUM (the 13 blocks are not mapped; the Post St blocks north of San Fernando between Almaden Ave and River St may also belong, the Post Office / Museum of Art and the plaza are not cleared). Dates MEDIUM. Traced 1915/1950 Sanborn fabric of the area: data/manual/sanborn/san_jose_downtown_*.geojson (sheets 86, 89, 90, 156).

name: Guadalupe Freeway (SR 87) corridor, I-280 to Julian St, along the Guadalupe River
note: State adopted the Guadalupe Parkway as a future freeway in 1963; construction allowed once City and County had acquired / conveyed the right of way (1965, 1969 statutes); Route 87 / I-280 interchange built 1972; a temporary 4-lane freeway from I-280 to Julian St built 1976; extended to Taylor St 1988; full freeway built 1997-2004 (cahighways.org). clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED 1970-1976 for the downtown stretch (some parcels may have been cleared in the late 1960s, the 1997-2004 widening took more). Ring = the freeway centre line (Overture 2026-10) buffered 50 m, not the real taking lines: extent LOW-MEDIUM. Prior fabric: River St / Pleasant St / Locust St cottages, lumber yards and the San Jose Water Co. shops along the river (Sanborn 1915 sheets 79, 87, 88, 156, 158).

name: Interstate 280 (Sinclair Freeway) through south downtown San José, SR 87 to US 101
note: 'The portion of Interstate 280 east from State Route 17 to U.S. 101 opened to traffic in mid 1972' (Interstate-Guide); 'Throughout the 1960s and 1970s, thousands of people in San Jose were displaced ... for the construction of Interstate freeways', some of the oldest neighbourhoods south-west of downtown under the I-280/SR 87 interchange (SJSU Mineta Transportation Institute, Beneath I-280, 2024). clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED 1965-1971 (right of way bought before the mid-1972 opening). Ring = the freeway centre line buffered 50 m (not the real taking lines): extent LOW-MEDIUM, dates MEDIUM.

name: Heinlenville (Sixth Street Chinatown), between 6th and 7th St, Jackson to Taylor St
note: Built by John Heinlen 1887-1888 on a ~5-acre pasture ('six blocks bounded by Sixth and Seventh streets'); after the Heinlen Company's 1931 bankruptcy the city bought the land and razed the neighbourhood for a municipal corporation yard, except the Ng Shing Gung temple, dismantled May 1949 (rebuilt in History Park 1991); yard closed 2006, Heinlenville Park opened 2023. clear_start/clear_end 1931 (temple 1949). Ring = 6th x Jackson, 7th x Jackson, 7th x Taylor, 6th x Taylor (Wikipedia coordinates 37.3514, -121.8939 fall inside): extent MEDIUM (the north / south limits Jackson / Taylor are from the Japantown descriptions, not a plat), dates HIGH. Not covered by the Sanborn tracing (vol. 1 sheets east of 5th St not traced).

name: Second Market Street (Plaza) Chinatown, Market Plaza block between San Fernando and San Antonio St (arson fire 1887)
note: Chinatown of 1872-1887 on 'most of the block along Market Plaza between San Fernando and San Antonio streets', destroyed by an arson fire on 4 May 1887 (the first Market Street Chinatown of 1866-1870 at the SW corner of Market and San Fernando burned in 1870). A fire, not a planned clearance: the block was rebuilt (1915 Sanborn sheet 89 block 1: Garden City Bank, Imperial Hotel, Post Office lot) and cleared again for the Fairmont Hotel (opened 1987; the Redevelopment Agency funded an archaeological excavation there in the 1980s). Ring = the four corners of that block (1st x San Fernando, 1st x San Antonio, East Market x San Antonio, Market x San Fernando at the Post Office lot) from the georeferenced 1915 Sanborn sheet 89 (fit RMS 1.9 m): extent MEDIUM, dates HIGH for 1887.

name: San José (McEnery) Convention Center blocks, San Carlos St to Viola Ave, Market St to Almaden Blvd
note: Convention centre approved by Mayor Tom McEnery in 1983 as part of an urban-renewal project that displaced a low-income Hispanic neighbourhood; opened 1989 (renamed McEnery 1991). clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED 1984-1987 between approval and construction. Ring = Market x San Carlos, Market x Viola, Almaden Blvd x Viola (lines extended), Almaden Blvd x San Carlos: extent MEDIUM, dates LOW-MEDIUM. Prior fabric on the 1915/1950 Sanborn maps (sheets 91, 92): Eagle Brewery, Columbia Hospital, Lincoln School, Swedish churches and frame cottages on Auzerais Ave / Viola Ave (data/manual/sanborn/san_jose_downtown_*.geojson).

name: Peralta Villa public housing (7th-8th St, Center St - Cypress St)
note: Oakland Housing Authority project, built c.1942 as segregated housing; the MacDermot mansion (on the 1911 Sanborn sheet 79 block 531, 'MacDermot properties') and the houses around it were razed in 1942. Extent from the oaklandwiki statement 'bounded by 7th, 8th, Center, and Cypress Streets'; the project may extend further north (LOW confidence for extent, MEDIUM for dates). Ring = centreline crossings Center/Mandela Pkwy (Cypress) x 8th/7th St (Overture).

name: Cypress Street Viaduct right of way (Cypress St / Mandela Pkwy, 7th St - 34th St)
note: Double-deck Nimitz Freeway (I-880) over a widened Cypress St: southern ramps completed Oct 1955, double-deck construction from Feb 1956, opened 11 Jun 1957 (collapsed 17 Oct 1989; right of way is Mandela Pkwy since the 1990s). FHWA (1998, via the urban-renewal atlas) counts ~600 families and dozens of businesses displaced. Cypress St was 60 ft on the 1911/1951 Sanborn maps; today's Mandela Pkwy right of way is ~55 m wide (half widths 25-30 m measured on Alameda County parcels north of 10th St), i.e. the frontage lots on both sides were taken. clear_start ESTIMATED (acquisition before the 1955 ramps), clear_end = construction start. Ring = Mandela Pkwy centreline (Overture) buffered 28 m between 7th St and 34th St (MEDIUM confidence for extent and dates). North of 11th St Cypress St did not exist in 1911: the freeway cut through whole blocks (Sanborn sheets 71, 57).

name: Oakland Main Post Office (1675 7th St) - blocks south of 7th St between Peralta St and Willow / Pine St
note: USPS distribution centre built 'roughly simultaneously' with the Acorn clearance (Schwarzer, Hella Town, 2021, via the urban-renewal atlas): about 12 square blocks of the 7th St corridor, ~400 Victorian houses plus storefronts. Dates ESTIMATED from that statement (MEDIUM-LOW). Ring = today's USPS parcel (Alameda County parcels APN 6-1-1-6, 7.2 ha), which covers the 1911 blocks of Willow, Campbell, Atlantic and Pacific St and the western 5th St (Sanborn 1911-12 sheet 92); MEDIUM confidence for extent.

name: Acorn urban renewal project (Union St - Brush St, 3rd St - 10th St)
note: Oakland Redevelopment Agency's first project (General Neighborhood Renewal Plan 1957, area named 1959): demolition April 1962 - May 1965, about 600 dwellings (more than 500 low-income families per Self 2003); the land lay vacant until the Acorn housing (groundbreaking 10 Nov 1967, first units 1969). Bounds quoted from the period: 'between 10th and First and Brush and Union Streets' / '45 blocks flanking the Nimitz Freeway between Union and Brush'; the residential core was 7th-10th St, Adeline-Market. Ring = Union/Brush x 10th/3rd St (centreline crossings; Brush x 10th from the West Oakland 10th St line extended, since the downtown grid meets the West Oakland grid at Brush St); the strip south of 3rd St (industrial) is not included. Includes industrial blocks that were not all cleared: apply the rule only to buildings without an exact year. Dates MEDIUM-HIGH, extent MEDIUM.

name: Oak Center redevelopment project (10th St - 18th St, Market St - Brush St; mostly rehabilitation)
note: Second West Oakland project after Acorn (redevelopment plan 1965, amended 1970). After the 1963-65 campaign of the Oak Center Neighborhood Association the agency committed (Feb 1965) that ~75% of the homes would be rehabilitated rather than razed; spot clearance followed (e.g. the Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School site, funded 1969). Dates ESTIMATED (1966-1972), boundary = the neighbourhood's usual limits north of Acorn (LOW confidence: no official project map was found). Apply ONLY to buildings with imputed / estimated years; most Victorians here survive.

name: West Oakland BART station block (7th St, Chester St, 5th St, Mandela Pkwy)
note: Station block bounded by Chester St, 7th St, Mandela Pkwy (Cypress St) and 5th St (Wikipedia); BART's Transbay line and West Oakland aerial were built in the mid/late 1960s and the station opened 16 Sep 1974 ('Oakland West'). The 1911 Sanborn blocks 493 / 494 (sheet 95: houses, W.P. Fuller warehouses, A.E. Howard planing mill) and the 1951 Goebel brewery blocks are on this site. clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED (MEDIUM-LOW); extent HIGH. Ring = centreline crossings.

name: I-980 (Grove-Shafter / John B. Williams Freeway) corridor between Brush St and Castro St, I-880 - I-580
note: About 503 homes in the freeway's path were demolished or moved (some Victorians to Preservation Park); a 1972 federal lawsuit halted construction until Caltrans agreed to build replacement housing; construction 1968-1985 (opened 1985). Route in the state system since 1947, freeway system 1959. clear_start/clear_end ESTIMATED from these (MEDIUM-LOW). Ring = today's I-980 centrelines (Overture, 'Grove Shafter Freeway' / 'John B. Williams Freeway') buffered 45 m between I-880 and I-580 (the blocks between Brush and Castro St; Brush and Castro are frontage roads).

name: City Center (12th St - 14th St, Broadway - Martin Luther King Jr. Way)
note: Oakland Redevelopment Agency 'City Center' project (planned from the late 1950s, scaled back from 70 to 12 blocks between 10th and 14th St west of Broadway): demolition ceremony 12 Nov 1970 (East Bay Yesterday), the Broadway Theatre demolished Nov 1972, first office tower at 14th and Broadway opened 18 Dec 1973, Clorox Building 1976; the Dellums Federal Building (12th-14th, Clay-Jefferson) followed in 1994. Ring = Broadway / MLK Jr. Way (Grove St) x 12th / 14th St centreline crossings; the 10th-11th St blocks are oak_convention_center. Dates MEDIUM (clear_end ESTIMATED), extent MEDIUM.

name: Oakland Convention Center and Hyatt Regency / Marriott (10th St - 11th St, Broadway - Clay St)
note: Two-block site bounded by 10th, 11th, Broadway and Clay St (1981 bid notice, PCAD); hotel opened May 1983, convention centre 1983. Clearance window ESTIMATED (before the 1981 bid; LOW-MEDIUM). Ring = centreline crossings.

name: Lake Merritt BART station and BART headquarters block (8th St - 9th St, Oak St - Madison St; Chinatown)
note: Building the station (under Oak St between 8th and 9th St, 800 Madison St) and the adjacent BART administration building 'leveled three blocks of Chinatown'; station opened 11 Sep 1972. Only the station / headquarters block is ringed (the other two blocks were not identified: LOW for extent); clearance window ESTIMATED from the construction period (LOW-MEDIUM). Not covered by the Sanborn tracing yet (1911 vol. 2).

name: Trans Pacific Centre block (10th St - 11th St, Broadway - Franklin St; T & D Theatre block)
note: Dense downtown block on the 1950 Sanborn (Oakland vol. 2 corrected to Nov 1950, sheet 151 block 143: shops, offices, printing, the 2,644-seat T & D Theatre of 1916 at 11th & Franklin). The T & D closed 1977 and was razed 1978 (PCAD; Cinema Treasures); the block is the only one east of Broadway left without the urban tint on the USGS Oakland West 1:24k photorevision of 1980 (1979 photos), i.e. cleared by 1979. Trans Pacific Centre phase I (1000 Broadway, 6 storeys) completed 1982 on about two thirds of it; 10th St between Broadway and Franklin was closed (not in today's street data). The Trans Pacific Centre was planned as 'a four-block square office and retail complex' across Broadway from the Hyatt / Convention Center site (SF Examiner 22 Nov 1981 via PCAD). clear_start/end from these dates (MEDIUM). Ring = centreline crossings (10th x Franklin interpolated).

name: Trans Pacific Centre phase II site, south block (9th St - 10th St, Broadway - Franklin St)
note: Fully built on the 1950 Sanborn (vol. 2 sheet 150 block 119: garages, stores, the Oakland Revival Tabernacle church hall, Hotel Ellis); still tinted (built up) on the 1979-photo revision of the USGS Oakland West sheet; part of the 'three of a four-block square site' of Trans Pacific Center phase II (Draft EIR, City of Oakland, SCH 1981120809, received 26 Feb 1982: a 68-storey tower and two 30-storey residential towers - never built). Clearance dated between the 1979 photos and the 1982 EIR (ESTIMATE, LOW-MEDIUM). The land stayed with the Oakland Redevelopment Agency, vacant / surface parking (ESTIMATE; in 2000 the agency sold the Franklin St part to SNK Development and bought back 135 of its parking spaces for public use, GlobeSt 30 Aug 2000) until the Courtyard by Marriott (988 Broadway, 2002) and the Franklin 88 (2004).

name: Pacific Renaissance Plaza / EBMUD double block (9th St - 11th St, Franklin St - Webster St)
note: Two built-up blocks on the 1950 Sanborn (vol. 2 sheets 150/151 blocks 120 and 142: plumbing supply and glass warehouses, a garage, lodgings, restaurants, the Travelers Hotel); still tinted on the 1979-photo revision; the eastern half of the four-block Trans Pacific Centre square (clearance dated as for the 9th-10th St block, ESTIMATE, LOW-MEDIUM). The redevelopment agency assembled the land and sold it for Pacific Renaissance Plaza (opened 1993; Oakland LocalWiki, Wikipedia 'Chinatown, Oakland') and the EBMUD administration building (375 11th St, dedicated 1991, Oakland LocalWiki); vacant / parking in between (ESTIMATE).
